title: "Quantitative & Population Genetics"
subtitle: "Foundations of Genetic Variation and Quantitative Trait Analysis"
---

## Course Overview

This course develops the theoretical foundations of population and quantitative genetics, with emphasis on the mathematical and statistical principles used to study genetic variation and complex traits.

We examine how genetic variation arises and is maintained in populations, how evolutionary forces shape allele frequencies, and how genetic and environmental factors contribute to phenotypic variation. The course integrates classical population genetics with quantitative trait analysis and modern approaches to trait mapping.

---

## Core Themes

### Population Genetics

- Measuring genetic variation (heterozygosity, nucleotide diversity, allele vs. genotype frequencies)  
- Gene pools and Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium  
- Mating systems and inbreeding  
- Mutation, migration, recombination, and linkage disequilibrium  
- Genetic drift and natural selection (directional, balancing, purifying)  
- Applications in conservation biology, medical genetics, and forensics  

### Quantitative Genetics

- Statistical modeling of complex traits  
- Partitioning genetic and environmental sources of variation  
- Broad- and narrow-sense heritability  
- Prediction of offspring phenotypes  
- QTL mapping and association mapping  

---

## Learning Objectives

After completing the course, students should be able to:

- Explain how genetic variation is generated and maintained in populations  
- Interpret Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium and deviations from it  
- Describe the effects of drift, selection, mutation, and migration on allele frequencies  
- Partition phenotypic variance into genetic and environmental components  
- Calculate and interpret broad- and narrow-sense heritability  
- Predict phenotypes from parental values  
- Design and interpret QTL and association mapping studies  
- Connect mathematical models with biological interpretation  

---

## Course Structure

This book contains the **core notes** of the course.

Each chapter includes:

- Conceptual explanations  
- Mathematical formulations  
- Worked examples  
- Computational demonstrations in R  
- Figures and simulation examples
